cards.front: Recall a key point about Component 1 Technique
cards.back: Component 1 examines Key Films in US and UK cinema, testing your ability to analyse and evaluate film language, representation and context.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Component 1 Technique
cards.back: Section A focuses on US film, requiring detailed knowledge of your set US film including its production context, genre conventions and representations.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Component 1 Technique
cards.back: Section B focuses on UK film, requiring understanding of your set UK film including its social context, institutional background and cultural significance.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Component 1 Technique
cards.back: Both sections include extract-based questions where you analyse a sequence using precise film language terminology and connect techniques to meaning.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Component 1 Technique
cards.back: The extract question typically asks you to analyse how micro features create meaning and generate response in a specific sequence from your set film.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Component 1 Technique
cards.back: Stimulus questions provide a still image or prompt and require you to discuss a relevant aspect of your set film using your own knowledge and examples.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Component 1 Technique
cards.back: Extended questions in Component 1 require you to evaluate aspects of your set films such as representation, genre or production context with sustained argument.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Component 1 Technique
cards.back: For US film, be prepared to discuss Hollywood studio context, genre conventions, star image and representations of characters, groups and issues.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Component 1 Technique
cards.back: For UK film, be prepared to discuss the British film industry context, cultural identity, social realism traditions and the film's relationship to its audience.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Component 1 Technique
cards.back: Always link your analysis of film language to the specific contexts required by the question: production, social or cultural context as appropriate.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Component 1 Technique
cards.back: Representations questions require you to discuss how characters or groups are constructed through film language and consider the implications of these constructions.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Component 1 Technique
cards.back: Practise timed responses to past paper questions, ensuring you can write sustained analytical and evaluative essays within the allocated time.
